clue.text: Award half-decent speech

indicators.note: half of a six-letter word means its first three letters are kept here

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict on a prizewinner's acceptance speech: only half-decent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-decent' looks like faint praise for the speech, but 'half' takes DEC from 'decent'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medal or order bestowed for service is a decoration, an honour given as an award.

clue.text: Obligation of French telecom company

parts.note: de is French for of
BT is British Telecom, the UK's main telephone company

explanation.surface: A query about a contract owed by a French phone firm.
explanation.walkthrough: BT (British Telecom) is the UK's former state telephone company.
explanation.definitionFit: Money one owes is a financial obligation, something one is bound to repay.

clue.text: Girl with unusually nice heart

indicators.note: unusually means arranged in an uncommon way, so the letters of nice and heart are mixed

explanation.surface: A description of a young woman who is uncommonly kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges NICE plus HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use a girl's first name for 'girl'; this is a common female forename.

clue.text: Perhaps write right verse

definitions.meaning: the pair of words 'write' and 'right' end in the same sound, an example of a chime between words
poetry with matching line endings, a jingle

explanation.surface: An instruction to a poet: compose proper poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'write right' looks like advice, but the two words are an example of the answer, flagged by 'Perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhyming poetry or a jingle is called verse, and two words with matching end sounds are an instance.

clue.text: Joint league leader?

definitions.meaning: a cut of beef roasted as a joint, taken from the upper leg
the team at the top of a league table

explanation.surface: Asks whether two teams sharing first place are joint leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective (shared first place) but is a joint of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Topside is a lean beef cut for roasting; the top side of a league is the team leading it.

clue.text: Food over at breakfast?

parts.note: O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
breakfast is an example of a meal, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Suggests some food is left over from breakfast time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground oats used for porridge are a staple foodstuff.

clue.text: 'Paddington's Home' screened by picture palace from the East End

indicators.note: reading from the east end means starting at the right-hand end and going leftwards
screened by means kept behind a screen, so the letters lie concealed within the words

explanation.surface: A film titled 'Paddington's Home' showing at an old cinema in London's East End.
explanation.walkthrough: The East End is a working-class district of London, but here it means read from the right. Backwards, picturE PALace gives the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington Bear came to London from 'darkest' South America, this country being his homeland.

clue.text: Mysterious meteoroid oddly missing base

indicators.note: with its odd-placed letters absent, only the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of meteoroid stay

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A puzzling space rock that has lost its launch site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly missing' leaves EERI from METEOROID; E is the mathematical constant, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Something eerie is strange and unsettling, inexplicable in a spooky way.

clue.text: See 14
Coward cut up over Scottish golfing resort

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second
in a down clue, up means the word is written bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to lop is to cut off
Troon is an Ayrshire town with a famous Open Championship links course

explanation.surface: Someone upset at a Scottish golf town is called a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut up' looks like 'upset', but 'up' turns LOP into POL in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A poltroon is an old word for an utter craven, a spineless person.

clue.text: Nuts quite like what a cricketer might hold

definitions.text: quite like what a cricketer might hold
definitions.meaning: a batsman holds a bat, and the suffix -y means resembling, so 'rather like a bat'

explanation.surface: A fond description of a cricket-mad eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Batty is informal for crazy; read as bat plus -y it means bat-like.

clue.text: Picked up something from Rome that smells nice

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a thing with a pleasant scent

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a receiver picks up a signal, so it is the spoken sound that counts

parts.note: popery is a hostile old word for Roman Catholic doctrine, something coming from Rome

explanation.surface: A souvenir brought back from Rome that has a pleasant fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like 'bought', but it asks for a word heard: POPERY, an old hostile term for Roman Catholicism, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of dried petals and spices kept to scent a room is a fragrant mixture.

clue.text: Air support on course to cover Matthew and son

indicators.note: to cover means to go around, so the golf peg is wrapped around the other pieces

parts.note: on a golf course a tee supports the ball
Levi is the other name of the apostle Matthew, the tax collector
s is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A golf broadcast about an air-supported ball and a father and son pairing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gospels call the tax collector Matthew 'Levi'.
explanation.definitionFit: To air a programme is to broadcast it, to put it out on television.

clue.text: Article with yours truly as subject

parts.note: the is the definite article
yours truly is a jokey way of saying me

explanation.surface: A writer boasting about a magazine piece all about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is the topic under discussion, what a piece is about.

clue.text: Strange haunting moves Trinity College

indicators.note: strange means odd or abnormal, so the letters of the three words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A ghost story: an odd haunting causes a Cambridge college to relocate.
explanation.walkthrough: Trinity College looks like the Cambridge college, but 'Trinity' is fodder and 'College' alone defines; the 20 letters of HAUNTING MOVES TRINITY are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A university in the East Midlands, loosely a college, a place of higher education.

clue.text: Men provided something cold for opening

parts.note: OR is Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers
provided means on condition that, if
ice is frozen water, certainly cold

explanation.surface: Soldiers bringing a chilled drink to an opening ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (Other Ranks) is the military term for enlisted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or vent, an opening in the body or a structure.

clue.text: Private centre

definitions.meaning: private here is an adjective meaning domestic, concerning one's own inner affairs
a centre is the inside or middle part

explanation.surface: Two words, perhaps a soldier at the middle of the formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier; here it is the adjective, as in a Minister of the domestic affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Interior means inward or domestic, and as a noun the inside middle of a space.

clue.text: Female with pride

parts.note: a group of lions is called a pride, so a she-lion is a female belonging to one

explanation.surface: A woman who is proud of herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like self-esteem, but it is the collective noun for a group of lions.
explanation.definitionFit: The female big cat lives in a pride, the social group of lions.

clue.text: Important German city Italy almost rebuilt

parts.note: Essen is a city in the Ruhr in Germany

indicators.note: rebuilt means constructed again in a new form, so those letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the final letter of Italy is dropped

explanation.surface: A German city and Italy, nearly reconstructed after war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Italy to ITAL, and 'rebuilt' rearranges that to TIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Essential means vital or indispensable, absolutely necessary.

clue.text: Support for the board?

parts.note: the board suggests directors, but it is a flat tabletop resting on a framework of legs

explanation.surface: Asks who will back the company directors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the board' looks like a company's directors; it is a plank or table top.
explanation.definitionFit: A trestle is a framework with splayed legs and a crossbeam, used to hold up a table top.

clue.text: Controversial European aim

parts.note: a motive is the aim or reason behind an act

explanation.surface: A disputed European policy objective.
explanation.definitionFit: An emotive issue stirs strong feeling, so it is contentious, likely to cause argument.

clue.text: Resent band's attitude

parts.note: to mind something is to object to it, resent it
a set is a group or band of people; the 's is read as 'is' joining to the definition

explanation.surface: Someone resenting a music group's arrogant manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's habitual outlook or way of thinking is their attitude.

clue.text: Chap I'm backing with each moving line

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the two letters are read right to left

parts.note: I'm gives the letters I and M

indicators.note: moving means shifting position, so the letters of each are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man supporting each new production line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses I'm; 'moving' rearranges the letters of each, giving CHAE, and 'line' adds the final L.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's forename stands for 'chap' in crosswords: any male, a fellow.

clue.text: Some man I certified gets better

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A doctor's note that a certified patient has improved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets better' looks like a verb phrase, but read as 'gets' (becomes) 'better', the comparative adjective, it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicer is the comparative of nice, more pleasant: better.

clue.text: Swear dog's evil at first

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog; with the 's it gives four letters

indicators.note: at first means the opening letter only of the following word

explanation.surface: A claim that a dog's wickedness shows from the very start.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, to utter oaths: swear.

clue.text: Owner of business backed worker accepting trophy

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the prize goes inside the other letters
backed means turned back, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business
an ant is a worker in crossword terms, from the worker ant
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A business owner whose employee receives a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the company abbreviation, and 'accepting' places the trophy inside that plus the insect worker, a stock crossword ant.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant is a person in possession of a home or post, its holder or owner.

clue.text: Group own all but the last two

indicators.note: all but the last two means every letter is kept except the final pair

parts.note: to own is to possess

explanation.surface: A collective that owns everything except the final two items.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but the last two' trims the final SS from POSSESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of people, originally summoned by a sheriff.

clue.text: Promise part of hospital will get oxygen for American

indicators.note: will get says the hospital area receives a new letter in place of an old one
for means in place of, marking which letter is swapped out

parts.note: a ward is part of a hospital
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A pledge that the hospital ward will get oxygen supplies for an American patient.
explanation.definitionFit: To give one's word is to make a solemn promise or pledge.

clue.text: Theatre regularly ignored Friends character? Blow it!

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, keeping alternate letters of theatre

parts.note: Monica Geller is one of the six friends in the American sitcom Friends

explanation.surface: A frustrated cry after a theatre company neglected a Friends role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly ignored' drops T, E, T, E from THEATRE, leaving HAR. 'Blow it!' looks like an oath; it is an instruction for the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouth organ is played by blowing into it, so 'blow it!' is its cue.

clue.text: Logs I ordered somewhere in Ireland

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new sequence, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Someone requested a delivery of firewood to a spot in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is a county and town in the north-west of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Look unpleasant for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: mean means unkind, unpleasant

explanation.surface: A performer gives the audience a nasty glare.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's mien is their bearing or expression, their appearance.

clue.text: Rich remark made to tailor for a job well done

definitions.text: remark made to tailor for a job well done
definitions.meaning: praise for a repairer who has put good heels on shoes

explanation.surface: A wealthy customer thanking a craftsman for good work.
explanation.walkthrough: The compliment really suits a cobbler, who heels shoes; 'tailor' is a slip, as a tailor makes clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-heeled is an idiom for wealthy, having plenty of money.
